name: Nkongho
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Hedinger, Robert (1987) The Manenguba Languages (Bantu A.15, Mbo Cluster) of Cameroon — comparative phonological coverage incl. Nkongho

new_statements.quote: From the PB roots and PM tones, it is clear that a second vowel must have been present in noun stems. Many of these vowels have been lost before and others since PM (cf. also 3.3.4 and end of 6.4.2). This may be described as a general trend which has been taking place over a long period of time. There appears to be no specific cause for this loss but it could possibly have to do with stress on the stem initial syllable. However, since tone is the main suprasegmental phenomenon which has distinctive function, stress is not often discussed and therefore the relationship of tone and stress is not well understood.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No synchronic word-stress rule is given for Nkongho (LEK) or any other variety. The languages are described as tone languages (phonologically H and L only, downdrift and downstep); the author merely conjectures, at the level of the Manenguba group as a whole, that historical loss of the stem-second vowel might reflect stress on the stem-initial (root) syllable, and states explicitly that stress is not discussed in the literature and its relation to tone is not understood.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the remark is a hedged diachronic conjecture, not a rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level (Manenguba cluster / Proto-Manenguba) comparative remark about noun stems; Nkongho (LEK, Mbetta village) is one of the 20-odd varieties in the correspondence tables and is formally excluded from Hedinger's definition of 'Manenguba' proper, though the V2-loss data include LEK. Not a statement about Nkongho citation forms or phrases.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: Hedinger's LEK = 'Lekongo/Nkongho (Kinkwa, Upper Mbo)', data he collected at Mbetta village (informants Foka Andrew Fontem, Fontem Nicholas) = Glottolog nkon1247 / ISO nkc. His stress conjecture is stated for the Manenguba group (Proto-Manenguba noun stems), not for Nkongho specifically, and he excludes LEK (with LEF Bafaw) from 'Manenguba' proper. The same passage was already recorded for sister targets baka1273 and bass1260 from the same on-disk files.
